Test-only: the repeated rows are `git` argument vectors and arms of a shell `gh` stub that model GitHub protocol responses. They are fixture data for one forged-comment scenario, not production dispatch logic.
URL/remote scheme detection uses '://' and ':' substring checks to decide whether a remote is already absolute; standard scheme handling, not a domain encoding.

Preflight is a sequence of four distinct validation steps (prompt assertion, authority refusal, freshness verdict, receipt); each branch is a separate gate, not a repeated identical shape.

Each branch validates a different typed model (initiative, definition, workspace, plan, graph) whose validate() has its own signature and error shape; there is no common row type to tabulate, and the graph arm maps violations rather than extending directly.

The arms match distinct EditAction variants with different bindings and different guard policies; the inner ifs each raise a differently named violation with its own message. A table would have to carry a closure per row and would hide which policy produced which violation id.

Shell-source scanner branching on distinct bash syntax prefixes (function / source / export) to bucket symbols, dependencies, and interfaces; the branches have different payloads, not one repeated shape.

The genuinely uniform part — the four signal penalties — is already a table with a single dispatcher loop. The remaining branches each apply a different scoring formula (flat credit, clamped coverage ratio, cache-hit rate, churn ratio) to a different field, so they share no row shape.

The branches are cumulative escalation thresholds, not parallel cases: each adds a different role set to the same accumulator, one arm removes a role, and one returns early. Order is semantic, so a predicate table would change behaviour.
Test module asserts on rendered conclusion lines and job names (build-test, audit, macos-test); literal CI-job identifiers, not a domain encoding.
Recursive-descent parser for cfg predicate compositions any()/all()/not(); each branch is a distinct grammar production, not repeated identical structure.

Counter aggregator over a match of distinct event types; the repeated saturating_add accumulation is the natural way to sum independent counters, not brute-force string logic.
Positional RFC3339 byte parser; the repeated branches check fixed-offset separator bytes ('-', 'T', ':') and are the format grammar, not copy-pasted logic.
Classifier matches protocol markers/identifiers by literal substring; protocol-string handling, not a domain encoding.
Top-level contract validate() delegating to one validate() per optional nested field; each call names a distinct field, not a repeated structural branch.
Metadata-block parser; each branch matches a distinct literal field prefix (issue:, ...) with its own payload handling, not one repeated shape.
Token parser for PR-reference forms (#N, HTML entities, /issues/N URL); each branch is a distinct reference grammar, not repeated identical structure.
